limits: Stress entries show raw peak tension (T) / compression (C). They are not qualified allowables or a safety factor.
The 0.454 kg departing-mass assumption gives 8.9044 N at 2 g; the preload sensitivity is 3 N total.
Maximum displacement changes across the finest two meshes are approximately 3.21% for the receiver, 0.99% for the adapter and 0.56% for the keeper. Only two receiver mesh levels were solved.
Raw stresses remain mesh-sensitive: the keeper axial fixture changes 29.5% in peak tension and 36.6% in peak compression; terminal-bearing compression changes up to 27.9% in the keeper.

The 12 N blocked-tip keeper case gives 1.173 mm maximum displacement in its deliberately unsupported fixture. It does not include the installed guide constraints and does not bound near-dead-center servo stall.
All parts use an isotropic effective-solid PLA comparison proxy, E = 2200 MPa and Poisson ratio 0.35. PAHT-CF directionality, print defects, creep and fatigue are not characterized.

Prescribed component contact tractions and rigid mounts do not solve assembled nonlinear contact, host flexibility, bolt slip, local yielding or dynamic release. Separate component displacement maxima cannot be added into an assembly-clearance claim.

Applied loads are the specified payload/contact forces and servo inertia in the vertical receiver cases. Distributed inertia of printed bodies, separate hardware inertia and harness loads are not modeled; the installation mass budget is separate.

Guide and sleeve friction coefficients are assumed. The coupled torque-demand calculation gives no measured servo margin. B03 compares required and available shaft torque through a consistent load path.

The uncalibrated tolerance stack can reach the open stop. Actual keeper calibration must leave at least 0.5 mm past the measured lug-clearance position and at least 0.5 mm before the actual open stop.
300 loaded-release trials, material/fit inspection, force/torque-profile measurements and power-loss tests remain unperformed. Numerical passes do not establish a flight-qualified payload rating.
